q: A lender asks about flood and heat risk at our factory. What do they want to know?
title: Answering a lender on physical climate risk
short: They want to know whether floods, heatwaves or water shortages could stop your plant or damage assets during the loan. Give your site's flood history, insurance cover, backup power and water, and any steps taken. Honest, specific answers help more than a generic policy.

ul: Past flood or waterlogging events and downtime.
Insurance policy and what it covers.
Plinth height, drainage and stock storage.
Heat effects on workers and machines, and cooling measures.

p: Supervisors expect banks to look at climate risk in their loan books. A plant that loses weeks to floods is a credit risk.
Photos, insurance claims and maintenance records back up your answers.

senseible: Senseible turns your bills into a dated, traceable emission record, the baseline a lender reads before it looks at a green project. Lenders decide; finance is never guaranteed.
